items.title: NEW — NAME COLLISIONS in a `[service]`/`[client_service]` expansion, B282's family not closed: an `[rpc]` method named `call` fails the build ("in code generated by this attribute: `call` expects 2 arguments, but got 4", spanned on the STRUCT) because the generated `<Name>Client` stub calls the imported FREE `call(self.transport, self.codec, ..)` from inside an impl that now declares `fun call`; a `[client_service]` method named `notify` fails the same way through `<Name>Proxy`; and `__request` (B282's gensym) is now the reserved parameter name — an `[rpc]` parameter literally named `__request` reproduces B282
items.discussion: rpc-smalls-32's finds F1 + F4 (2026-09-11); `reply`/`arg` checked safe (called from the dispatcher impl, which declares no such method)
items.body: Two fixes, pick one per name: QUALIFY the free calls in generated stubs (`rpc::call(..)`, `rpc::notify(..)` — the import list at rpc.vl ~4993 is where the unqualified names come from) so a user method of the same name cannot shadow them; or REFUSE the colliding names at the attribute in the method's vocabulary (one row, two names + the `__` prefix). Qualifying is the honest fix (it removes the hazard instead of naming it); the `__` prefix is a refusal either way (a user cannot be asked to know the generator's bindings). Pins: `[rpc] fun call(self, what: str): str` round-trips; `[client_service] fun notify(self, what: str)` round-trips; `[rpc] fun f(self, __request: str)` refused.

items.title: NEW — INTERNAL ERROR from two `KeyedCell::new([])` sites: a `[service]` struct with TWO exposed `KeyedCell<str, Task>` fields, both constructed `KeyedCell::new([])`, fails with "internal: a call resolved to `Keyed`'s requirement `key`, which has no body … please report this program" — ONE such field compiles (`9a0f031f`), and seeding either list with an element compiles; bites `[expose(keyed)]` × 2 and `[expose(keyed)]` + `[expose]` alike
items.discussion: rpc-smalls-32's find F2 (2026-09-11); repro in that lane's scratch; smells like an unsolved `T` from `[]` unifying across two sites under the `Keyed<K>` bound — solver territory
items.body: Reproduce with the lane's program (two `KeyedCell<str, Task>` fields, both `KeyedCell::new([])`, both exposed); find why the empty-literal element type at the second site resolves a `Keyed` requirement call to the TRAIT's bodiless declaration instead of `Task`'s impl (B254/B258's name-keyed-candidates family is the first suspect; the `[]` seed leaving `T` unbound until the field type lands is the second). Pin the two-field shape green, and the internal-error text as a must-not-fire.

items.title: NEW — an unresolved name in an impl SUBJECT is reported TWICE: `impl Source<Option<Nope>>` → two `Error:` lines for one mistake, where `let x: Option<Nope>` reports once — the subject is walked twice in `Node::Impl` (`walk_trait_position_type_node(subject, ..)` and again per argument for `impl_subject_args`) and each walk preps its own `prepped_type_locals` entry; pre-existing (it is how `impl Source<Option<_>>` drew its refusal twice at 65af4be0)
items.discussion: smalls-32's find F1 (2026-09-11); the house rule B189/B236 enforce elsewhere: one mistake, one report
items.body: Walk the subject once and reuse its locals for the argument pass, or dedupe the resolution diagnostic by (span, name) at the second walk. Pin: one error for `impl Source<Option<Nope>>`; the `let` form as the control.

items.title: NEW — an ANONYMOUS binder has no name for a diagnostic to use: `impl Pair<_: PartialEq, _: PartialEq>` with `self.first == self.second` reports "`_`'s `eq` accepts `_`, but the right operand is `_`" — three distinct parameters all rendered `_`. B186's nameless generics already get an `impl Bound` face (`operand_label`/`implicit_binder_bound`); routing anonymous binders through it would read `impl PartialEq` — but that function's own doc records that two `impl X` still collide, which is trait-typed-fields.md rev 2's Q3, the owner's
items.discussion: smalls-32's find F2 and open Q1 (2026-09-11); rec: yes for a bounded `_`, behind the Q3 ruling
items.status: OPEN — Order 32's finds (2026-09-11); OWNER Q (trait-typed-fields.md rev 2 §Q3)
items.body: Rule Q3 (how two `impl X` faces are told apart in a message — by position, by an ordinal, by the bound's argument), then route `_` binders through `implicit_binder_bound`. Until then the three-`_` message stands; pin the current text so the change is visible.

items.title: NEW — a BARE-TRAIT IMPL SUBJECT parses and then refuses every use of `self`: `impl Source<type I: Source<type U>> { fun flatten(self) .. }` is accepted at the head, but inside the body `self` is a bare trait type — "cannot call 'sub' on a value of bare trait type 'Source': a trait is not a value type (vilan has no trait objects)" — so the spelling is a trap: it means nothing a body can use, and the working spelling is `impl type S: Source<..>` one token away
items.discussion: reactive-32's A86 probe (2026-09-11); the owner's own probe head `impl Source<Option<type _: Source<type U>>>` compiles for the same reason and would fail at the first `self.` use
items.body: Either REFUSE the head (a trait in impl-subject position with a steer: "write `impl type S: Source<..>` to implement for every source" — one row) or make it MEAN that (desugar `impl Trait<args> { .. }` to `impl type S: Trait<args> { .. }`, the universal reading every other bare-trait value position already has — B186 parameters, B184 fields). The second is the consistent one and costs no new spelling; the first is smaller. Owner's call; pin either.

items.title: NEW — a BLANKET over a NESTED bound does not resolve: `impl type S: Source<type I: Source<type U>> { fun flatten(self): SignalCell<U> }` (MaybeSignal's shape, one level deeper) — (a) at ONE level the trait's own argument is not bound from the receiver (`let joined = outer.flatten()` → "never fully determined"; annotating the result makes it compile and RUN correctly), and (b) with the NESTED bound the receiver resolves to no concrete impl at all: "internal: a call resolved to `Source`'s requirement `get`, which has no body" — even for a fully concrete `SignalCell<SignalCell<i32>>` with the result annotated; the same one-level gap leaves `T` uninferred for `impl type S: Source<Option<type T>> { fun or(self, initial: T) }` although an ARGUMENT fixes it
items.discussion: reactive-32's A86 probe (2026-09-11) — A86 (`flatten` as a blanket over the trait) is BLOCKED behind this; two `#[ignore = "A86: …"]` pins in `inference/traits.rs` are the exhibits (`a86_an_inherent_blanket_over_a_trait_binds_its_argument_from_the_receiver`, `a86_a_blanket_over_a_nested_bound_resolves_its_receiver_to_a_concrete_impl`)
items.status: OPEN — Order 32's finds (2026-09-11); A86 waits on it
items.body: Two defects in impl selection over a bounded subject: the bound's ARGUMENT (`I`, `T`) is not solved from the receiver's instantiation when the subject is `type S: Trait<arg>` (B268 fixed the dropped-argument matching; this is the binding half), and a bound whose argument is itself bounded (`type I: Source<type U>`) resolves the requirement call to the trait's bodiless declaration (B296's shape from the other side). Un-ignore the two pins; then A86 lands as written.

items.title: NEW — `[derive(Wire)]` still EMITS `Json`/`FromJson` beside Wire (`derive_impl_source`'s `"Json" \| "Wire"` arm — "additive beside the JSON impls until the codec re-plumb consumes it"), so a Wire FIELD must also be Json and the message says nothing about Wire: `[derive(Wire)] struct Row { tags: Map<str, i32> }` fails "cannot find 'from_json_value' in Map<str, i32>" / "has no method 'to_json'" on stock 65af4be0 (`Map` has been Wire since A39); after B289/A82 the same residue reaches `Result` and every hand-written `impl .. with Wire` — `Result` works as an `[rpc]` RETURN (kolt store.vl:184's case) but not yet as a derived FIELD
items.discussion: wire-32's find F1 (2026-09-11); pinned as CURRENT behaviour in `a_derive_wire_field_typed_map_meets_the_same_pre_existing_json_residue` and `a_derive_wire_field_may_be_a_hand_implemented_wire_type`; the one half of A82 the lane could not deliver
items.body: Finish the codec re-plumb the arm's comment promises: `[derive(Wire)]` emits the Wire visitor impls alone (the JSON pair only under `[derive(Json)]`), and the derive's field check reads the Wire predicate (B289's) — so a `Map`, a `Result`, a user Wire type all sit in a derived struct. Flip the two current-behaviour pins to the admit face; a `[derive(Json, Wire)]` control keeps both.

items.title: NEW — a closure PARAMETER is not typed from an INHERENT IMPL METHOD's expected closure type: `View::link_to` in router.vl written with `\|event\|` fails a process build ("cannot call method 'prevent_default' on E"; reds `inference modules::ssr_process_build_can_import_a_browser_module_that_binds_on_event` and `platform::a_function_requiring_two_layers_renders_one_line_each_in_label_order`) while the BYTE-IDENTICAL body as a FREE FUNCTION compiles; `\|event: Event\|` fixes it — kolt's `on:contextmenu(\|event: Event\|` workaround from the 2026-09-11 freeze investigation is this bug

items.body: Inside an inherent impl method the callee's expected closure type (`on_event`'s `|Event| void`) is not applied to the closure parameter before the body is walked, where the same call from a free function is; find the impl-method path that skips `infer_closure_args_against_params`' fill (the `Self`-substitution context is the suspect), pin the un-annotated `link_to` body green on both platforms.

items.title: NEW — `Owner::release()`: after B291 an `Owner` is SINGLE-USE (a `take`/`defer` after `dispose` releases on the spot), so dispose-then-REFILL on one owner is gone; nothing in std/examples/docs/kolt did it (every boundary mints a fresh owner) and the one shipped pin that did was rewritten — but an app that wants a releasable-and-refillable owner has no verb for it
items.discussion: reactive-32's open Q1 (2026-09-11); rec: add `release()` (run the cleanups, stay live) only when a caller appears — the pattern is a smell (a boundary that outlives its content is what fresh owners are for)
items.body: If wanted: `fun release(self)` runs and empties the cleanups WITHOUT raising `disposed`; `dispose` = release + the flag. Doc the difference at `Owner`. Pin: release-then-take keeps the item alive; dispose-then-take releases it.

items.title: NEW — `when`/`swap` never REMOVE their live element on boundary disposal: they assume the parent subtree leaves the DOM with the boundary, which is false for a PORTAL whose parent stays — kolt `lib/overlay.vl:528–543` hand-writes `get_owner().defer(\|\| live_panel.read()?.remove())` with a comment saying exactly this; A71's `Region::close` is now the natural hook (A71 deliberately did not change disposal semantics)
items.discussion: ui-32's find F3 (2026-09-11); a ruling: is 'the boundary removes what it placed' the contract (then `Region::close` removes the live content and the overlay's defer goes), or 'the parent's removal is the app's' (then document it)?
items.body: Rec: the boundary removes what it placed — `Region::close` removes the live element/run and the anchor, on every form (`when`, `swap`, `bind_each`, the reactive arms); the cost is one `remove` per region at disposal, paid today by hand in kolt's overlay. Pin: a `when` inside a portal whose parent survives leaves nothing behind after the owner disposes; `ssr_differential` unchanged.
